applies_why: The judge text sets an issue to UNDERDETERMINED because the cited verse text does not name whose body is the channel, which is using a verse's non-statement as the ground.
quote: the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: The phrase 'does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for ... UNDERDETERMINED' can be read as barring silence about a detail from grounding UNDERDETERMINED, or as allowing UNDERDETERMINED when the text leaves a detail unnamed; I adopt the first because the rule expressly forbids non-statement as a ground.
why: The judge's stated reason is that the text does not name the channel, which is exactly the forbidden use of a verse's non-statement to support UNDERDETERMINED.
